Subject: Redwood SDK Quickstart — Post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samantha / Alex —

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about TechFin's plans to add LLM-based document QA + an embeddings-based reranker for search boosting. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of needs we heard
- Primary use case: document QA + customer support summarization (short answers + source attribution)
- Secondary: semantic search with embeddings + reranker to surface high-precision hits for billing and contract retrieval
- Architecture constraints: prefer VPC/private hosting for production, but willing to start on hosted for PoC; data residency requirement: US initially (may expand to EU)
- Integration priorities: SDK quickstart (Python/TS), auth model, routing to Dedicated vs Hosted, structured output/tool-calling for retrieval augmentation, embedding + reranker tuning

Deliverables we proposed
1) Redwood SDK quickstart package (Python + TypeScript) with local env setup and sample app — attachment: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf
2) Network diagram for PoC including required ports/CIDR — attachment: network_diagram.png
3) Integration checklist: auth options (API key, short-lived tokens for Private), sample code for embeddings and reranker, example tool-calling JSON for structured outputs
4) Follow-up technical sync (30 min) next week to confirm infra details and finalize PoC plan

Immediate next steps (action owners)
- Marissa: share quickstart package, sample apps, and a link to the GitHub samples (by EOD today) — DONE (see attachments + drive link)
- Dev: produce a minimal sample project that includes local testing with the Python SDK and a Dockerfile for the service (ETA Mon 3/23)
- TechFin: confirm whether you want to start on hosted (fastest) vs Private (VPC) for the PoC and share any firewall/CIDR constraints

Notes about auth & routing (short)
- Hosted (Redwood API): API keys + fine-grained per-key scopes; easiest for PoC
- Dedicated/Private: short-lived pods tokens and KMS/HSM integration for keys; we'll provide token exchange examples in the quickstart
- Smart routing: you can route by latency/cost/region — we'll include a simple policy example that routes sensitive traffic to your Dedicated pool

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf (quickstart + sample app links), network_diagram.png
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123 (sample repo), HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/48291

Thanks — I’ll book the follow-up once you confirm preferred PoC environment.

Best,

Samantha — thanks, answers inline and a few quick examples below.

1) Auth / Private token exchange
- Quick answer: the SDK repo includes an example token-exchange service (Node + Python examples). For hosted PoC you can just use an API key set as REDWOOD_API_KEY in env. For Private we provide a short-lived token flow: client requests a token from your auth service -> exchange on backend for a scoped short-lived token via our auth endpoint. We’ll attach the token-exchange example in the repo.

2) Local testing / .env
- Example .env (Python):
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
  REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.com/v1
  REDWOOD_ENV=dev
- Dockerfile in sample project runs uvicorn + mounts .env; we’ll include docker-compose for a local Postgres + vector extension (pgvector) example.

3) Embeddings + reranker pipeline (Python example)
- Generate embedding:
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  emb = client.embeddings.create(input=[text])
- Store vector in Postgres (pgvector) with document id and metadata
- Retrieval: nearest-neighbor query in Postgres -> return top N doc ids
- Rerank: call Redwood Ranker (reranker model) with candidate doc texts + query; returns scores used to reorder top N before generation
- We have a sample script in the repo: samples/embeddings_rerank.py that wires these steps together.

4) Structured output / tool calling
- We include a function-calling example for retrieval augmentation: you can return structured JSON for {answer, sources:[], followup_needed:bool}. The SDK supports both explicit function-calling and a schema-driven JSON output mode — we’ll include both examples.

Links / repos
- Quickstart PDF (attached) includes links to GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples (samples for Python & TS)
- Direct sample files: samples/python/quickstart_app.py and samples/ts/quickstart_app.ts

Timeline & next meeting
- We can deliver a hosted-PoC sample (with local Docker + sample Postgres) by EOD Mon 3/23. Dev will own the sample project.
- Proposed demo windows: Tue 3/24 10–11am PT or Wed 3/25 2–3pm PT — which works for you?
